sentences: Crop Common bean | Country Tanzania | Title Preventing Sulphur deficiency in Common bean (Guinea savanna) | Text Sulphur deficiency in common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris). Preventing it in the Guinea savanna, with one long rainy season and moderately fertile soils: Include sulphur-bearing fertilisers in the programme and build organic matter to supply slow-release sulphur. In the Guinea savanna, time operations to the single rains, top-dress at the onset of steady rainfall, and use the long season for a full-duration variety. | Source AGRA

Crop Maize | Country Kenya | Title Identifying Zinc deficiency in Maize | Text Zinc deficiency in maize (Zea mays). How to recognise it in the field: Interveinal chlorosis (yellow stripes between green veins) on the YOUNG upper leaves, shortened internodes giving a rosette or 'little-leaf' look, and in maize a broad white-to-yellow band on either side of the midrib. | Source AGRA

Crop Maize | Country Ghana | Title Correcting Zinc deficiency in Maize (Highlands) | Text Zinc deficiency in maize (Zea mays). Correcting it in the cool highlands, where heavy dew and mild temperatures favour foliar fungal diseases: Apply zinc sulphate to the soil or as a 0.5% foliar spray on young plants; seed treatment with zinc also helps short-season cereals. In the highlands, the long dewy nights drive foliar disease, so prioritise resistant varieties, wider spacing for airflow, and early scouting. | Source National Extension Service

widgetData.source_sentence: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: How do I fix nitrogen deficiency in pearl millet?
sentences: Crop Pearl millet | Country Nigeria | Title Correcting Nitrogen deficiency in Pearl millet (Guinea savanna) | Text Nitrogen deficiency in pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum). Correcting it in the Guinea savanna, with one long rainy season and moderately fertile soils: Top-dress with urea (46% N) or CAN, splitting the rate so part goes on at planting and the rest at active vegetative growth. A foliar urea spray (1-2%) gives a fast green-up. Incorporate well-rotted manure or a legume green manure. In the Guinea savanna, time operations to the single rains, top-dress at the onset of steady rainfall, and use the long season for a full-duration variety. | Source ICRISAT

Crop Pearl millet | Country Niger | Title Telling Nitrogen deficiency in Pearl millet apart from look-alikes | Text Nitrogen deficiency in pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum). How to tell it apart from similar deficiencies: Because Nitrogen is mobile in the plant, the symptoms appear on the OLDER, lower leaves first. This separates it from immobile-nutrient shortages such as zinc, iron, sulphur or boron, whose symptoms strike the YOUNGEST upper leaves. Confirm with a soil or leaf test before treating. | Source AGRA

Crop Groundnut | Country Malawi | Title How Groundnut Rosette Disease spreads in Groundnut | Text Groundnut Rosette Disease of groundnut, caused by virus complex (aphid-transmitted). How it spreads: Transmitted by the groundnut aphid; late-planted and widely spaced sparse stands suffer most. | Source IITA

Growth is slow, roots are poorly developed, maturity is delayed and grain filling is weak. | Source FAO

Correcting it in the humid forest zone, where heavy rainfall leaches and acidifies soils and fungal pressure is high: Apply zinc sulphate to the soil or as a 0.5% foliar spray on young plants; seed treatment with zinc also helps short-season cereals. In the humid forest, correct soil acidity with lime, watch for rapid fungal spread under the canopy, and improve drainage on the heavy leached soils. | Source ICRISAT

Crop Maize | Country Ghana | Title Preventing Phosphorus deficiency in Maize (Humid forest) | Text Phosphorus deficiency in maize (Zea mays). Preventing it in the humid forest zone, where heavy rainfall leaches and acidifies soils and fungal pressure is high: Apply P as a band near the seed rather than broadcasting, correct soil acidity with lime, and build organic matter, which holds P in plant-available forms. In the humid forest, correct soil acidity with lime, watch for rapid fungal spread under the canopy, and improve drainage on the heavy leached soils. | Source IITA

widgetData.source_sentence: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: How do I manage rice blast and bacterial leaf blight in rice?
sentences: Crop Rice | Country Madagascar | Title Management of Rice Blast Disease Caused by Magnaporthe oryzae | Text Rice blast disease, caused by the fungus Magnaporthe oryzae, leads to significant yield losses in rice production worldwide. A recent study focused on developing a mechanistic simulation model for rice blast using STELLA 9.1 software, based on the EPIRICE model from IRRI. The model integrates leaf and neck blast submodels, utilizing a linear regression equation to establish their relationship. Verification was conducted using data from eight sites, with validation at five locations in the Philippines. Graphical comparisons indicated that simulated and observed leaf blast severity and neck blast incidence curves were similar. Statistical validation employed the Wilcoxon test, Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and equivalence tests. Results showed low RMSE values for leaf blast severity and higher values for neck blast incidence. The Wilcoxon test revealed significant differences in leaf blast severity predictions, achieving 60% accuracy for neck blast predictions. However, the equivalence test indicated only 40% accuracy for both leaf blast severity and neck blast incidence, highlighting the complexities of these pathosystems. Potential leaf blast epidemics were mapped in Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, and the Philippines using projected weather data. | Source CGIAR

Crop Maize | Country Zambia | Title Impact of Site-Specific Nutrient Management Recommendations on Maize Production | Text In Sub-Saharan Africa, agricultural extension has struggled to enhance technology adoption and productivity growth among farmers. A study conducted in northern Nigeria focused on the effectiveness of site-specific nutrient management recommendations for maize production. The research involved a randomized controlled trial with smallholder farmers, analyzing the impact of two extension treatments: recommendations with and without additional information on output price variability and expected returns. The findings revealed that site-specific recommendations improved fertilizer management practices and maize yields, although they did not significantly increase overall fertilizer use. Notably, recommendations that included information on expected returns led to greater fertilizer investments that continued beyond the initial year. However, the overall increases in investments and net revenues were modest, indicating that while targeted advice can enhance practices, the effects on productivity and investment levels remain incremental over the treatment period. | Source CGIAR

Crop Rice | Country Tanzania | Title Management of Rice Blast and Bacterial Leaf Blight | Text Rice blast and bacterial leaf blight (BLB) are significant diseases that threaten rice yields across all growing regions under favorable conditions. A genome-wide association study (GWAS) involving 147 rice accessions identified 23 significant marker-trait associations (MTAs) related to these diseases, corresponding to 107 candidate genes for blast and 210 for BLB. The haplo-pheno analysis revealed eight superior haplotypes for blast, with average SES scores from 0.00 to 1.33, and five superior haplotypes for BLB, with scores ranging from 1.52 cm to 4.86 cm. Notably, haplotypes LOC_OS12G39700-H4 and LOC_Os06g30440-H33 showed the lowest average blast scores, while LOC_Os02g12660-H39 had the lowest average lesion length for BLB. A total of ten accessions for blast and eight for BLB were identified, belonging to aus and indx subpopulations from Bangladesh, Brazil, India, Myanmar, and Pakistan, as well as eight accessions from six countries for BLB resistance. | Source CGIAR

widgetData.source_sentence: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: What fertiliser should I use for rice?
sentences: Crop Maize | Country Nigeria | Title Preventing Maize Stem Borer on Maize (Humid forest) | Text Maize Stem Borer (Busseola fusca / Chilo partellus), a pest of maize. Preventing attack in the humid forest zone, where heavy rainfall leaches and acidifies soils and fungal pressure is high: Destroy crop residue that harbours larvae, plant early, and use push-pull or resistant varieties. In the humid forest, correct soil acidity with lime, watch for rapid fungal spread under the canopy, and improve drainage on the heavy leached soils. | Source IITA

Crop Rice | Country Tanzania | Title Fertiliser recommendation for Rice | Text Fertiliser programme for rice (Oryza sativa). Apply phosphorus and potassium basally and split nitrogen into three: at transplanting/establishment, active tillering, and panicle initiation. Avoid blanket high nitrogen, which worsens blast and blight; aim for balanced ~100-120 kg N/ha by leaf-colour chart. | Source CGIAR

Crop Cowpea | Country Ghana | Title Fertiliser recommendation for Cowpea (Humid forest) | Text Fertiliser programme for cowpea in the humid forest zone, where heavy rainfall leaches and acidifies soils and fungal pressure is high. As a nitrogen-fixing legume, cowpea needs little nitrogen; apply a phosphorus-rich basal (SSP or DAP) to feed nodulation and add potassium on depleted soils. In the humid forest, correct soil acidity with lime, watch for rapid fungal spread under the canopy, and improve drainage on the heavy leached soils. | Source FAO
